headline: Trainable, but 5 images lack label files — 2 of them in val, which will corrupt your validation mAP; create the missing .txt files (empty if truly background) before training.
training_impact: Training will not crash: Ultralytics treats an image with no .txt as a pure background image. The cost is silent, not fatal. The 3 unlabelled train images teach the model that any objects in them are background, suppressing recall for those classes. Worse, the 2 unlabelled val images (val/000000223182, val/000000549220) are scored as background: if they contain objects, your validation mAP is measured against a corrupted set and the number you use to make the go/no-go decision is wrong. Everything else (geometry, normalisation, class IDs, leakage, image integrity) is clean.

decisions.rationale: 5 images have no label file: train/000000006040, train/000000226147, train/000000322610, val/000000223182, val/000000549220. Exact detector, verified — the .txt files are genuinely absent. Two are in val, so this is the one finding that can invalidate your validation metric, not just degrade the model. Fix: open each image; if it is a genuine background scene, create an empty .txt; if it contains objects, annotate it. Do this before training, and re-run the structure scan to confirm 468/468 and 132/130→132/132 pairing.

3 train label files contain zero rows: train/000000211120, train/000000242934, train/000000368335. Empty labels are a legitimate background-image technique, so this may be intentional — but an accidentally emptied file is a silently dropped annotation. Visually confirm the three images are true backgrounds; if not, re-annotate. Low urgency: 3 of 468 train images, no effect on the val number.

3 label files with no matching image: train/398764888884, train/531232685887, train/654553082395. These are never read during training — pure dead weight, likely remnants of deleted/renamed images. Delete them for hygiene; zero impact on training or metrics.
